name: Design and Media
overview: You work across visual communication, industrial design and digital design, starting with design fundamentals, strategic identity and sustainable design, and moving into thematic studios. Teaching is hands-on and process-based, mixing workshops, seminars and group projects with feedback sessions, and the third year ends with a bachelor's thesis; exchange and internships are encouraged. Later you choose a track such as Collaborative and Industrial Design, Fashion and Textile Design, Creative Sustainability, New Media, or Visual Cultures and Contemporary Art. Graduates work in communication, interaction, product, service and strategic design, or continue to a master's.

name: Economics
overview: The programme combines economic theory with mathematics, statistics and programming, and the first year includes a course on big societal issues such as inequality, ageing, migration and climate change. You build your own study plan with a minor, for example data science, and can spend a semester abroad at a partner university. Teaching is on campus in Otaniemi, a short ride from central Helsinki, and the degree ends with a bachelor's thesis under a faculty supervisor. It is linked to the Helsinki Graduate School of Economics, and graduates become analysts, consultants, advisers or researchers, with a place in the Aalto master's programme.

name: Finance
overview: You study financial markets, investment analysis, risk management and corporate finance, backed by quantitative methods and data analytics, and learn how firms are valued and capital is allocated sustainably. Courses lean on teamwork and cases, with guest lectures and company collaboration, and a closing course looks at the role of finance in society before the bachelor's thesis in year three. A flexible minor can come from technology, design or economics, or you can swap it for an exchange. The student association Aalto Finance runs events and trips to financial centres. Graduates become analysts, consultants and portfolio managers, and continue to the Aalto master's in finance.

name: International Business
overview: You learn marketing, accounting, management, entrepreneurship and business ethics, then pick a theme package such as global supply chains, entrepreneurship, marketing or people management, with data analysis running through the courses. Real business cases, group projects and presentations are the main way of working, and an exchange semester abroad is built into the degree, followed by a capstone course. Electives can come from other Aalto schools, and options include an IT minor or the selective Aalto Founder School. Graduates work as project or business development managers, marketers, consultants and entrepreneurs, and the degree leads into the Aalto master's in business.

name: Chemical Engineering
overview: The first years cover mathematics, programming, machine learning, chemistry, physical chemistry and biochemistry, with a focus on sustainable processes in bioproducts and biotechnology. You learn through lectures, group work and laboratory courses, moving from guided exercises to more open projects, with industry guest lecturers and a bachelor's thesis. Electives point towards master's paths in biotechnology, chemical and metallurgical engineering, or chemistry and materials science, and exchange is possible at partner universities. Graduates enter the chemical, semiconductor, biotech, food, pharmaceutical and electronics industries, or go on to research.

name: Computer Engineering
overview: You combine mathematics, physics, programming and electrical engineering with computer science, covering computer architecture, low-level programming, microelectronics, embedded systems and signal processing, plus themes such as AI, the Internet of Things and network security. Lectures and seminars go together with frequent group work and lab projects, including work around a RISC-V microprocessor built by Aalto students. Exchange studies and internships abroad are options. Graduates continue to master's studies in electronics or computer and information sciences, or work as software, hardware, network or embedded engineers.

name: Data Science
overview: The first year builds foundations in mathematics and programming, the second deepens them with optimisation, statistical inference and machine learning, and the third brings a bachelor's thesis, a seminar and optional advanced courses. Lectures are paired with project work, so you practise building data-driven models that make predictions. The degree draws on Aalto's research links with the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence and on collaboration with companies and research institutes. Graduates work as data scientists, engineers or technology entrepreneurs, and the master's route leads to computer science or mathematics and operations research.

name: Digital Systems and Design
overview: You study networking, control and automation, electronic circuits, embedded systems and machine learning, programming in languages such as Python, C++ and Matlab, and you add design thinking and electronic prototyping. Multidisciplinary team projects, industrial projects and a hands-on final project tied to the thesis give you practical experience, and part of the degree can be taken abroad on exchange. The mix of electrical engineering and design is the programme's particular character, and you work alongside students from business, arts and computer science. Graduates go on to the Aalto master's in electrical engineering or to roles in automation, electronics and simulation engineering.

name: Mechanical and Civil Engineering
overview: You study applied mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, statistics, numerical methods), engineering fundamentals such as fluid mechanics, thermodynamics and mechanics of materials, and computing, including programming, algorithms and finite element methods. The distinctive angle is numerical simulation and programming applied to mechanical and civil problems. You solve real engineering challenges in team projects, use industrial engineering software and finish with a thesis; a semester abroad or summer courses at partner universities are possible. Master's options include mechanical engineering, civil engineering, geoengineering and advanced energy solutions, leading to work as structural, energy or naval engineers.

name: Technology, Business and Design
overview: You study mathematics, programming, strategic management, corporate finance, global economics and design process skills, with a focus on responsible, sustainable technology. In the first year you choose a major in technology (mechanical and civil engineering, computer and data science, or digital systems and design), in business, or in design and technology. Teaching combines team projects, industry collaboration and iterative design work, a year-long product development project in the design track, and a bachelor's thesis, with minors and electives to tailor the degree. The programme connects to Aalto's startup community, and graduates go into software, data science, product design, consulting and founding companies.

name: Information Technology
overview: The programme centres on software development with an emphasis on artificial intelligence, structuring and analysing big data, web, mobile and cloud platforms, and graphic design with a user-experience focus. From the second year you choose between Intelligent Robotics, which covers social robots, user-centred design and sensor data, and Data Processing and Analytics, which covers data management, scalability and predictive analytics. Practical skills are built from the start, with internships and close work with industry partners, and the small campus has real robots on site. Graduates work as AI specialists, software and web developers, project leaders and analysts.

name: International Business
overview: You study how business operates in global settings, with sustainable practice, digital tools and analytics, leadership and presentation skills. After the first year you specialise in Strategic Marketing and Consumer Insights, Logistics and International Trade, or Accounting, and you can add development studies such as entrepreneurship or creative marketing. Teaching uses lectures, workshops and case studies done alone and in groups, plus guest lectures, project collaborations with companies and a work placement in Finland or abroad. Exchange periods are available, and graduates become marketing managers, supply chain coordinators, financial analysts or consultants, start their own companies, or study a master's.

name: Mechanical and Sustainable Engineering
overview: The degree joins engineering, sustainability and digitalisation, with attention to sustainable materials and design. You learn to spot sustainability opportunities through circular-economy thinking, choose suitable materials, use 3D design and simulation tools, and explore computer vision and robotics for more efficient production. Work happens in a production laboratory and in departmental projects with internal and external partners, supported by company visits, internships and a thesis done with a company. Teachers are close to students, and the programme runs beside a Swedish-language track. Graduates work as mechanical, design, production, process or sustainability engineers.

name: Quantum Technology
overview: The major joins quantum physics, mathematics, computer science and electrical engineering, covering quantum materials, circuits and information processing, plus programming, electromagnetic fields, machine learning and quantum laboratory experiments. Lectures, seminars, group and project work run alongside hands-on lab work, including experiments with the AaltoQ20 quantum computer. It is run jointly by the schools of Science and Electrical Engineering, with research ties to VTT and the EU Quantum Flagship. Graduates work as quantum computer engineers, chip designers, software developers and algorithm engineers, or continue to a master's in quantum technology, materials physics, electrical engineering or computer science.

name: Degree Programme in Aviation Business
overview: You study air transport management, airline and airport operations, revenue management, air cargo and safety and risk management, along with service design, branding, human resources leadership and logistics. Teaching uses interactive classes and real projects with international aviation stakeholders, and you can do an internship or exchange abroad before finishing with a thesis. The school has close to 200 partner institutions worldwide, studies run by day on the Porvoo campus, and there is an online option for people working alongside. Graduates go into airline and airport operations, cargo logistics, revenue management, customer experience and travel services.

name: Degree Programme in Business Information Technology
overview: The degree joins business and IT, and you pick one of four specialisations: Software Development (full stack, back end or front end), ICT and Business (solution consulting or data analytics), Digital Services (including 3D development), or ICT Infrastructures, Cloud Services and Cybersecurity. Studies are arranged with partnering IT companies, so you work on projects with local and international firms in multicultural teams, and finish with a thesis. Teamwork and communication skills are developed along with the technical ones. Graduates become software developers, digital service designers, cloud specialists, business developers, IT consultants or IT project managers.

name: Degree Programme in Digital Business Innovations
overview: You study digital business ecosystems, data-driven marketing and futures thinking, along with innovation, prototyping, the Internet of Things and the basics of AI. Complementary courses cover graphic design, web development, project management, user experience, branding, marketing analytics and data analytics with Python. You work on real company projects and start networking with firms from the first semester. Classes are on the Porvoo campus, which has students from around 50 nationalities. Graduates work as digital marketing specialists, content designers, e-commerce specialists, digital sales managers and business innovation specialists.

name: Degree Programme in International Business
overview: You build a broad understanding of business in a global and digital setting, then choose a major in Accounting and Finance, People Management, Marketing and Sales, or Supply Chain Management, with language studies throughout. Teaching works closely with companies and uses student-centred methods; you can study full-time by day or in a blended format with evening classes. Exchange studies abroad are encouraged and a thesis is written in your major field. The degree is based in Pasila, Helsinki, and holds EFMD programme accreditation. Study paths are flexible, with professional courses that can be drawn from different majors.

name: Degree Programme in Sports Coaching and Management
overview: The programme focuses on sports coaching, sports management and event planning, with a strong emphasis on ice hockey coaching. You study athlete-centred coaching, coach development, sports administration and event organisation, and put it into practice by coaching youth teams in local clubs and assisting coaches on campus. Study plans are personalised with tutors, and a work placement in the third year takes place in an organisation of your choice. The campus at Vierumaki is Finland's largest sports education centre, and the programme works with the International Ice Hockey Federation and the Finnish Ice Hockey Association. Graduates go into coaching, club administration, event management and sports entrepreneurship.

name: Immersive Software Engineering and AI
overview: You study software engineering, artificial intelligence and mathematics, along with entrepreneurship and business and integrated Finnish language, society and culture. Instead of traditional lectures, you learn in small collaborative groups guided by academic experts, exploring concepts through activities modelled on real working life, with weekly progress tracking. Two four-month internships in developing modern IT systems are part of the degree, and paid places are available through participating companies. Graduates become R&D engineers, software developers or architects, technology consultants, product managers or entrepreneurs, or continue to master's and doctoral studies.

name: Early Childhood Education
overview: The degree covers early childhood education pedagogy, with children's development and growth, play-based learning and cooperation with families at its centre. Finnish language studies are woven through the modules, so you learn in a functionally bilingual way and develop an understanding of bilingual and multilingual education in Finland. The approach draws on Finland's emphasis on supporting children's agency and participation. Graduates qualify as early childhood education and pre-primary teachers in Finland, and can continue to the master's programme in educational sciences for wider career options.

name: Degree Programme in Hospitality and Tourism Experience Management
overview: You study experience design theories and modern design processes, gamification and imagineering, within a major in Experience Management, and add an optional minor in hospitality, tourism, experience design or business. Learning is built on hands-on projects and real cases with companies, a work placement, language studies and a bachelor's thesis. Exchange is available with partner universities in countries including Spain, Portugal, Japan and South Korea, and placements abroad are possible. The school belongs to the THE-ICE tourism and hospitality education network. Graduates work as experience specialists, event managers, food and beverage managers, hotel managers and in people and culture roles.

name: Business Innovation and Sustainability
overview: You study the management of business innovation, sustainable management, new business creation, decision-making and the sustainability transition, with electives in digital marketing, responsible management and entrepreneurship. Related disciplines include accounting, commercial law, corporate communication, environmental management, economics, marketing and strategy. Courses run in smaller groups with direct contact with faculty, you follow a personal study plan, and exchange and company traineeships are options. Graduates work in consulting, corporate responsibility, sustainable business and sales, or continue to master's programmes in international business, environmental management or digital marketing.

name: Service Experience Management
overview: You combine hospitality management, service design, and leadership and business, then add a focus in Innovating Food Services, Tourism Service Development or Event Service Production. Service design methods are taught through classroom studies and working-life projects, with team projects on real business challenges and shifts in BarLaurea, the teaching restaurant, where you work both as staff and as process planner. A work placement and a thesis showing workplace expertise complete the degree, and study visits abroad add an international angle. Graduates work as project managers, event producers, restaurant managers and service design planners, or continue to a master's in service innovation and design.

name: Cyber Security, Business Information Technology
overview: You learn to secure systems, analyse risks and prevent threats, alongside project management, communication, problem-solving and business administration. Teaching follows Laurea's Learning by Developing model, with hands-on projects, real development assignments, laboratory and simulation environments for testing vulnerabilities, and workshops with business experts; PwC and Microsoft appear among partners. The curriculum uses the competency frameworks that security professionals work with internationally, and you collaborate with students from other fields. Graduates work as information security specialists, threat analysts, systems developers, security coordinators or cybersecurity consultants, or continue to a master's.

name: Developing Digital Services, Business Information Technology
overview: You study business fundamentals, programming and software development basics, databases, infrastructure, information security, service design methods and analytics, from requirements analysis through application design, implementation and testing. You choose between the Cloud Developer and Digital Service Designer tracks. Teaching is online, with webinars, workshops, project work and optional campus sessions, plus two practical placements and a final thesis or project with a working-life organisation; Industry 4.0 projects touch robotics, IoT, data analytics and VR. Graduates work as IT consultants, web, mobile and application developers, data analysts, product owners and project managers.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: You study structural engineering in steel, timber and concrete, sustainable materials, building information modelling and data management, infrastructure such as energy systems, water management and transport, and the built environment in society. Teaching mixes lectures, exercises, company visits, projects and laboratory work, including exercises in virtual environments and materials laboratories, and the final semester is a bachelor's thesis research project. You study alongside students of Sustainable Construction Technology, with cooperation from LAB University of Applied Sciences and industry; teaching is mainly in Lahti. Graduates work as structural and infrastructure engineers, BIM specialists, development managers or urban planners.

name: Electrical Engineering (HEBUT double degree)
overview: This double degree covers mathematics, physics, engineering design, mechanics, electronics and control systems, then moves into power systems, electrical drives, circuits, digital design, mechatronics and embedded systems. Alongside the engineering, you study basic Chinese, Finnish and English, and can add a minor such as energy economics or innovation and entrepreneurship. Lectures, exercises, laboratory work, company visits and projects lead to a bachelor's thesis, and you complete the whole degree in Finland while earning certificates from both LUT and Hebei University of Technology. Graduates work as project, test, design and technical sales engineers, or continue to master's studies at LUT.

name: Business Management
overview: You study business communication, marketing, leadership, data analytics, financial management, sales development and sustainability, and choose a track in either Corporate Financial Management or Digital Marketing. Teaching follows the Learning by Developing approach: authentic projects with companies, up to two work placements, and a final development project usually done with a partner company. Industry certifications from Microsoft, Google and SAS are built into the coursework, and double-degree options exist with partners in Austria and Belgium. Graduates become digital marketing specialists, financial planners, business developers, project managers or entrepreneurs.

name: Nursing
overview: You study nursing theory together with clinical practice in surgical, internal medicine, mental health, paediatric and rehabilitation settings, including safe medication handling, ethical decision-making and client-centred support, with Finnish courses geared to nursing. Skills are first practised in simulation and then applied with supervised patients across several placements; the thesis is a development project, usually with a healthcare partner. A dual-degree option with Nazareth University lets you spend a year in the United States. Graduates work as registered nurses in hospitals, clinics, home care, occupational health, mental health and public health, or in humanitarian roles.

name: Social Services
overview: You study working with clients in social services, service systems, social work methods and the development of client-oriented services, across the lifespan from children and families to older people, mental health, substance abuse and disability. Training is practical, with three internships of at least ten weeks in different settings, projects with organisations, and a development project usually done with a service provider, NGO or municipality. Study is blended, mixing campus sessions with online learning. Graduates work as social counsellors, family and youth workers, school counsellors or specialists in mental health and substance abuse, or continue to a master's in global health and crisis management.

name: Chemical and Process Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, chemistry, physics and renewable energy together with separation technologies and process development, covering chemical reactions, mixing and flows with applications in biorefineries, water treatment and food processing. Teaching combines extensive laboratory work, lectures, company visits and group projects, and ends with a bachelor's thesis. Process design, simulation, AI and safety are part of the toolkit, with a focus on sustainable production and the circular economy. Graduates work as process designers, environmental specialists or development engineers, or continue to master's programmes in energy transition, food processing or water technology.

name: Computational Science and Artificial Intelligence
overview: You study mathematics, statistics, computer science, numerical methods and programming, then specialise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, matrix calculus, optimisation and partial differential equations, with minors such as software engineering, energy economics or business management. Teaching combines lectures and exercises with company visits, projects, extensive laboratory work and a bachelor's thesis. Mathematics and computer science are merged to solve practical problems with algorithms and data analysis. Graduates work as data analysts, data scientists, machine learning engineers and AI specialists, and can move on to the master's programme in data-centric engineering.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: You study electrical energy systems, electrical machines, electronics, embedded systems and mechatronics, on a base of mathematics, physics and programming, with practical skills in measurement and design. Teaching combines lectures and exercises with extensive laboratory work, company visits and projects, and you can add a minor such as energy economics or sustainability science. Graduates work as electrical, test, embedded systems and project engineers in energy, manufacturing, technology and transport. The degree leads to master's programmes in electrical engineering, electric transportation systems or renewable power-to-X economy, or to double-degree master's options in Wroclaw or Hannover.

name: Energy Technology
overview: You study thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, nuclear power engineering, power plant engineering and energy economics, covering how electricity and heat are produced from solar, wind, thermal and nuclear sources. Mathematics, physics, design, control systems and programming support the core, and minors include electronics and sustainability science. Teaching uses lectures, extensive laboratory work, company visits and projects, and ends with a bachelor's thesis. Nuclear safety studies are offered only at this university in Finland. Graduates work as development and design engineers, reactor engineers and nuclear safety specialists, or continue to a master's in energy conversion, nuclear engineering or sustainable energy systems.

name: Energy Technology (HEBUT double degree)
overview: This double degree covers engineering design, programming and electricity, thermodynamics, nuclear power engineering, power plant engineering, energy economics and sustainability science, organised around physical phenomena, energy conversion and the machinery used for it. Teaching combines lectures, extensive laboratory work, company visits and projects, ending in a bachelor's thesis. You complete the whole degree in Finland and receive certificates from both LUT and Hebei University of Technology. Graduates work as development engineers, design engineers, reactor engineers and energy consultants, or continue to master's programmes in energy conversion, nuclear engineering or sustainable energy systems.

name: Environmental Technology
overview: You study engineering mathematics, physics, chemistry, programming, thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, then life cycle assessment, sustainable cities, wind and solar technologies, climate solutions and the circular economy. Teaching mixes lectures with individual and group projects, laboratory work, modelling assignments and company visits, using real challenges from industry, cities and society. You choose a minor such as energy economics, international business or computational science. Graduates work in environmental management, sustainability assessment, climate action, clean technology and urban development, or continue to master's programmes in circular economy or sustainability science.

name: Industrial Engineering and Management
overview: You study industrial engineering and industrial economy on a base of mathematics, physics and software engineering, then specialise in areas such as innovation management, product and service development, entrepreneurship, business analytics, supply chain management and marketing, with attention to digital transformation and sustainability. Teaching combines lectures, company visits, projects and laboratory work, with close industry collaboration that opens internship opportunities, and a thesis in the last semester. Graduates work as industrial engineers, supply chain and investment analysts, quality engineers and business controllers, or continue to master's programmes in innovation, logistics or organisational development.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, physics, engineering design, mechanics, materials and control systems, then specialise in mechatronics, robotics, production engineering, finite element analysis and machine design, with attention to digital design environments and the product life cycle. Teaching combines lectures, exercises, projects and extensive laboratory work, and students can use the Jamie Hyneman Center prototyping lab. Minors include energy economics and sustainability science. Graduates work as design engineers, production managers and product development engineers in machinery, automotive, energy and healthcare, or continue to master's programmes in industrial design engineering, materials science, mechanical engineering or mechatronics.

name: Mechanical Engineering (HEBUT double degree)
overview: This double degree with Hebei University of Technology covers engineering physics, mathematics, mechanics, 3D engineering, materials, energy systems, measurement and control, robotics, mechatronics and AI-driven machinery, with Chinese language study throughout. Teaching combines lectures, company visits, projects and extensive laboratory work, including the Jamie Hyneman prototyping lab, and ends with a bachelor's thesis. A minor can be energy economics, sustainability science or Chinese business and culture, and you receive degrees from both universities. Graduates work as design engineers, production and quality managers and product development engineers in automotive, energy, food, healthcare and construction.

name: Software and Systems Engineering (HEBUT double degree)
overview: You study object-oriented programming, discrete mathematics, data structures and algorithms, computer networks, cybersecurity, web applications and IoT-based systems, plus basic Chinese, Finnish and English. Teaching combines lectures, company visits, projects and extensive laboratory work, and the degree closes with a bachelor's thesis; the curriculum stresses sustainable development and digital transformation. It is a double degree with Hebei University of Technology, taught entirely in Finland, with certificates from both universities. Graduates work as software developers, testing and automation engineers or business analysts, or continue to master's programmes in software engineering or digital systems.

name: Technology and Engineering Science
overview: You start with engineering mathematics, physics, mechanics, thermodynamics, 3D modelling and technical documentation, linking mechanical, electrical, energy and environmental technology with IoT skills. In the intermediate studies you choose a direction: energy technology, electrical engineering, environmental technology or mechanical engineering. Teaching combines lectures, company visits, projects and extensive laboratory work, and the degree holds EUR-ACE and ASIIN accreditation. It opens the way to many English-language master's programmes in energy, electrical, mechanical and environmental engineering, or to careers as engineers, project managers and sustainability consultants.

name: Digital Business
overview: You study digital business models, digital sustainability, business information systems, AI applications, data-driven management and digital transformation, alongside accounting, finance, economics, leadership and marketing. Studies are on campus in Lahti with lectures, company visits and practical projects, a minor in industrial engineering or software and information systems, and a research-based bachelor's thesis; exchange periods are encouraged. Graduates work as digital marketing specialists, product or service managers, business developers and analytics or transformation specialists, or continue to master's programmes in international business and entrepreneurship, international marketing or supply management.

name: Sustainable International Business
overview: You study accounting, finance, economics, management and strategy, then specialise in international business, sustainable business, international entrepreneurship, international marketing and purchasing, or professional sales. Sustainability is treated as a driver of changing business models, and extensive language, communication and diversity studies build a multicultural outlook. Lectures, exercises, company visits and projects are the main ways of working. Graduates work as business development, international sales, supply chain or export managers, or continue to master's programmes in international business and entrepreneurship, supply management or international marketing.

name: International Business and Logistics
overview: You study supply chain management and the operations of international trade, and choose a professional major in either Supply Chain Management or Marketing, with electives in finance, human resources and strategic management. Teaching combines interactive lectures, business simulation games, company field trips, real cases and projects, together with a work placement and a thesis. Exchange studies are possible at over 60 partner universities, and a double degree with HTW Saar in Germany gives you two bachelor's degrees. Graduates work as procurement specialists, logistics coordinators, supply chain analysts, marketing managers and entrepreneurs, or continue to a master's in Finland or abroad.

name: 3D Game Art
overview: You learn to use 3D graphics to produce images, animations, special effects and real-time applications, alongside 2D motion graphics, traditional visual arts and visual design, with character design, animation, VFX and compositing as core areas. Teaching is learning by doing: practical exercises and production groups that imitate workplace practice, large collaborative projects, and final-stage work often done with representatives from the industry. The programme is based on the Arabia campus, a creative district of Helsinki. Graduates work as 3D animators, character designers, VFX artists and architectural or product visualisers in games, film and television, advertising and design agencies.

name: Game Design
overview: You learn to design and produce games in collaborative development teams, covering visual design, interactive storytelling, game mechanics, 3D graphics, virtual environments, character design, programming, AI technologies and extended reality. Teaching happens in production teams that simulate real industry environments, with client-based projects and studio work in industry-standard game engines and 3D software, in an intensive full-time model. The programme builds on Metropolia's earlier XR design education and encourages responsible use of AI. Graduates work in game development, interactive media, simulation, entertainment and digital storytelling, in game studios, design agencies, marketing and educational content.

name: Sustainable Fashion Business Management
overview: You study international fashion business, branding and fashion communication, consumer behaviour and trend forecasting, product and merchandising development, and the use of data and technology in business, with sustainability throughout. The programme approaches business specifically from the perspective of the fashion and textile industry, including its global supply chains. Teaching is work-integrated, with projects, collaboration with industry partners and assignments tied to real working life. Graduates work as fashion business specialists, brand development experts, sustainability coordinators, merchandising managers, trend analysts and marketing specialists, or as entrepreneurs.

name: Civil Engineering and Building Services
overview: You study the broad foundations of construction and building services, with a major subject in civil engineering or building services, and develop problem-solving, mathematical and economic thinking, teamwork, IT and communication skills, with sustainable development and digital literacy as themes. Learning is by doing, through problem-solving and cooperation, with a practical work training period and a bachelor's thesis; classes are by day at the Myllypuro campus, and international students learn Finnish alongside engineering. Graduates work as civil or HVAC engineers in engineering and design firms, construction companies, the building products industry, public administration and research institutes.

name: Electronics
overview: The degree starts from the fundamentals of electronics, with the physics and mathematical analysis behind them, and builds toward options in embedded systems design, sensor technologies, radio technology, wireless communications, and electronics design and testing, alongside project management, sustainable development and communication skills. The first two years lean on theory and the later years on applied project work, with a large amount of practical exercises and projects. Study is on the Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa. Graduates work as design and technical specialists, application engineers, technical sales and project managers in communications, consumer electronics, medical devices and automation.

name: Information Technology
overview: After orientation studies you choose a major in Software Engineering, with paths in software, game, mobile or web development covering programming, databases, machine learning and cybersecurity, or in Smart IoT Systems, which focuses on designing, building and securing IoT devices and networks. Mathematics, physics and English support the core, and every course has a substantial coding component with a major project each semester. The study model is intensive and full-time on campus, with industry projects, a work placement and a final year project. Graduates work as software engineers, game, mobile and web developers, or in product development and technical support, and many continue to a master's.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: You build mathematical and scientific foundations and apply them in practical engineering, then choose a major in Machine Design, which covers product development, materials, manufacturing and computer-aided design, or in Aircraft Engineering, which covers aeronautics, aeromechanics, structures, avionics, engines and drones. Theory is combined with practical projects and a work placement that can be partly or fully abroad, followed by a thesis, and international exchange is part of the programme. Finnish language support helps with life and networking in Finland. The Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa hosts the programme, and graduates move into industry or on to a master's.

name: Robotics Engineering
overview: You study robot software, mechatronics, robotics systems, robot perception, and robot control and learning, supported by mathematics, automation, artificial intelligence and mechanical engineering, with entrepreneurship and AI as themes across the degree. The blended format mixes periodic classroom days, small group work, online teaching and independent study, so it can be done alongside work. You learn by doing, take part in Metropolia's research and development innovation hubs, and do excursions, work placements and thesis projects with local and multinational companies. Graduates work as robotics, automation, project and design engineers and technical sales engineers in manufacturing, healthcare, agriculture, logistics and aerospace.

name: Smart Automation
overview: You study electronics, programming, computer science and electrical engineering, with cyber-physical systems, digital twins and AI and machine learning for automation, combining mechanical and electrical thinking. Real-world projects with Finnish companies let you work on industry challenges, and the skill set reaches beyond software into smart manufacturing, sustainable energy systems, intelligent logistics and smart healthcare. The programme is based at the Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa and prepares you for Industry 5.0 and digitalisation. Graduates work as automation engineers, IoT developers, machine learning engineers, control engineers, smart manufacturing specialists and AI and automation consultants.

name: International Business and Analytics
overview: You study finance, accounting, marketing, supply chain management and international business, with a professional major in Business Analytics and electives such as human resources and strategic management. Sustainability reporting, corporate responsibility and innovation projects run through the curriculum. Teaching uses interactive lectures, company field trips, real business cases and multidisciplinary projects with other Metropolia programmes and companies, followed by a work placement and a thesis. Exchange is possible at over 60 partner universities. Graduates work as data analysts, business analysts, digital transformation specialists and sustainability reporting specialists.

name: Construction Site Management
overview: The programme trains you to lead construction work as a site manager, with basic studies in mathematics, sciences and languages, vocational studies in construction and a specialisation in house construction. You learn to plan and run a construction site and to supervise construction professionals. Classes are by day and taught in English and Finnish, with an innovation project commissioned by a company in the field, a work placement and a thesis. The degree meets the legal competence requirements for site management in Finland. Graduates work as site managers or in expert roles in construction services, customer service and property management.

name: Biomedical Laboratory Science
overview: You study taking samples, point-of-care testing, clinical histology and cytology, clinical chemistry and haematology, microbiology, genetics, physiology, neurophysiology and nuclear medicine, building laboratory technique and understanding of human cell biology. The degree combines professional studies, hands-on laboratory training, group work, virtual learning and Finnish language courses, with internships spread across the programme, some in the school's own laboratory, and a thesis that can be done with a working-life partner. It is taught mainly in English and designed for international students. Graduates work in hospitals, research laboratories and diagnostic centres, where Finnish is needed for employment.

name: Nursing
overview: You learn clinical nursing skills, communication and decision-making, teamwork in multiprofessional groups and how to organise your work, with professional Finnish language developed step by step alongside. Teaching combines theory, clinical skills training and simulation in a simulation hospital with emergency, intensive care, surgical and paediatric environments, with contact teaching on campus. The bilingual programme is designed for immigrants who start from basic Finnish and study together with Finnish speakers. Graduates become registered nurses working in hospital wards, emergency, intensive care, home care, private health services and health technology, or continue to a master's in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.

name: Occupational Therapy
overview: You study occupational therapy, health and rehabilitation, how daily activities affect health, assessing participation in everyday life and applying client-centred methods, with work-life projects and a bachelor's thesis. Teaching is blended, combining campus sessions, live online classes, independent study and group work, with practical training in real work environments over four semesters and a personal study plan. The programme stresses evidence-based practice and working with other professions, and Finnish learning is encouraged to support placements. Graduates work in health care and rehabilitation, schools and early childhood education, mental health, occupational health and community organisations.

name: Paramedic Nursing
overview: You study emergency care and the treatment of patients of all ages in varied environments, together with general nursing skills and Finnish language studies, so that you qualify as both a paramedic and a registered nurse under EU professional qualification rules. Teaching combines theory, clinical skills labs and simulations in advanced spaces including a simulation hospital and an ambulance, with about a third of the degree in clinical practice with patients, plus innovation studies and a bachelor's thesis. The programme is bilingual, so no prior Finnish is needed to start. Graduates work in ambulances, emergency rooms, intensive care and acute care, or continue to a master's in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.

name: Public Health Nursing
overview: You qualify as both a public health nurse and a registered nurse, studying through theory lessons, practice in skills labs, simulation exercises, language studies and a bachelor's thesis, with Finnish taught from the first semester. About a third of the degree is real healthcare placements, and training uses simulation spaces including a simulation hospital and the HyMy Village. Teaching is bilingual, mainly in English, with international projects and exchange opportunities. Graduates work with people of all ages in maternity clinics, school health services, occupational health, primary care, home care and hospitals, or continue to master's studies in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.

name: Social Services
overview: The degree is built on a social pedagogical approach: empowering citizens, preventing marginalisation and promoting inclusion. It develops five areas of competence, which are ethics in social work, client work, knowledge of social service systems, critical and inclusive citizenship, and research and development skills. Teaching uses lectures, group work, workshops, projects, e-learning and three to four internships in different social service settings, and an early childhood education specialisation is an option. It is taught mainly in English while you learn Finnish. Graduates work in child welfare, family work, youth guidance, school counselling, elderly care, disability services, mental health and substance abuse work.

name: Laboratory Science
overview: You learn chemical and biological laboratory methods applied to food safety, water and air quality, forensics, quality assurance, detection of disease-causing microbes and instrumental analysis, with electives in sustainability, programming, leadership, procurement or languages. About half of the contact teaching takes place in well-equipped laboratories, and project work with external partners complements it. A five-month internship in a company or research institute and a thesis done with a partner organisation complete the degree. Graduates work as laboratory analysts, quality specialists, researchers and validation specialists, or continue to a university master's in chemistry or biology.

name: Applied Gerontology
overview: You study the foundations of gerontological expertise, the right to individual ageing, supporting a good life for older people, older people in the home environment, promoting participation and wellbeing, and person-centred guidance. The degree combines campus teaching, independent online study, projects with working-life partners and practical training in real work settings, with Finnish learned along the way. It is taught mainly in English and aimed at international students and immigrants who want a career in Finland. Graduates work as gerontology specialists, social and client counsellors, home care coordinators and service advisers in the public, private and non-profit sectors.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: You study cooperation and interaction with the client, assessment of functional ability, human body structure and function, biomechanics, motor learning and therapeutic exercise, with applied exercise, aquatic therapy, water rescue training and Finnish language studies throughout. Teaching mixes blended learning, group work, lectures and supervised clinical practice, some in the school's own HyMy Village facilities, and a bachelor's thesis that can be done alone or in small groups with workplace partners. Instruction starts in English and moves toward bilingual delivery. Graduates qualify as licensed physiotherapists and work in hospitals, health centres, private wellbeing and rehabilitation services, or as entrepreneurs.

name: Software Engineering
overview: The curriculum moves from programming fundamentals to web and mobile development, user interfaces, usability and software regulation, and on to artificial intelligence, data-driven systems, cloud computing and cybersecurity, with sustainability, ethics and responsible technology use woven in. The programme combines technical skills with collaboration, problem-solving and communication, and prepares you to work in international and multidisciplinary environments. Graduates can work as software engineers, developers, architects, consultants, data or AI engineers, web or mobile application developers and cloud solution specialists.

name: International Business
overview: You learn core business theory and apply it, choosing two specialisation modules from eight options: Accounting and Finance, Digital Business, Experience Economy, Human Resource Management and Leadership, Innovation Management and Business Development, Digital Marketing, Supply Chain Management, and Sustainable Entrepreneurship. First-year students run a Virtual Firm, and later work comes through case studies, company projects and team assignments, led by coaches, with a study period abroad as a required part of the degree. Double-degree partners are in Belgium, France and Germany. Graduates work in marketing, sales, supply chain management, project management, consulting and entrepreneurship in Finland and abroad.

name: Business in Finland
overview: The programme joins a broad business foundation with studies specific to Finland: Finnish corporate culture, business practice and legislation, with compulsory Finnish language learning built into the coursework rather than set apart. The first year introduces business in Finland, the second deepens competence through applied projects, the third offers professional exposure and the fourth ends with a bachelor's thesis, with elective professional studies and free-choice courses along the way. It is aimed at international students who want to build a career in Finland, and it addresses gaps employers have identified in graduates' knowledge of Finnish workplace culture.

name: Team Entrepreneurship
overview: You study leadership and management, sales and marketing, financial management, teamwork, and the creation of new services, products and business models, and develop skills such as collaboration, communication, emotional intelligence and critical thinking. Rather than classes in the usual sense, you learn through teamwork, dialogue and weekly reflection guided by professional team coaches, running real businesses as a co-founder, working with actual clients and building projects that earn revenue. The pedagogy has over 25 years of history in entrepreneurship education, and the programme forms an entrepreneurial community of alumni, coaches and business partners. It prepares you for a path as a founder or leader.

name: Bilingual Degree Programme in Nursing
overview: You study foundational nursing and move to advanced clinical care, from patient safety, ethical and client-centred care and everyday nursing work to clinical reasoning and evidence-based decision-making, with Finnish language study built into the professional courses. The programme is functionally bilingual, starting mainly in English and bringing in more Finnish as it advances, and it includes extensive supervised clinical placements in real healthcare environments. It serves people who do not yet speak Finnish and leads to an EU-recognised qualification as a registered nurse. Graduates work in primary and specialised health care and the private sector, in hospitals, health centres, companies and non-profit organisations.

name: Automation and Robotics, Science and Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, natural sciences and engineering foundations, then focus on designing and developing automation and robotic systems, programming intelligent machines and applying data, sensing and digital technologies to real problems; a minor subject complements your specialisation in the second year. Learning combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, with company collaboration and practical assignments, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates find work in manufacturing, energy, transport, healthcare and logistics, and the bachelor's degree leads straight into master's programmes at the same university without a new application.

name: Biomedical Engineering, Science and Engineering
overview: The programme combines engineering, biology and health sciences, with a focus on biomedical instrumentation, biomaterials, tissue engineering and molecular biology. The first year covers mathematics and natural sciences, and the second introduces the biomedical engineering specialisation plus a minor of your choice. You learn through projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, build teamwork skills, and can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates go into healthcare technology, medical device development, and research and innovation, and the bachelor's degree continues to several master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

name: Environmental Engineering and Green Transition
overview: The programme prepares international engineers for the energy and environmental industries, with a practical focus on waste and water treatment and on investigating and monitoring contaminated soil, water and air. Study topics include ecosystems, soil and groundwater, water and sanitation, ecotoxicology and waste management, so that industrial and public production processes can be run sustainably. You learn to carry out sampling and analysis in the field and in the laboratory, in an international community, and degrees of this kind usually include a practical training period and a final thesis. Graduates usually work with process, water, waste and environmental monitoring tasks in industry, utilities and consultancies.

name: Early Childhood Education and Care
overview: You combine theory and practical skills in social services, early childhood education and social pedagogy, with special attention to intercultural communication and language development, and Finnish as a second language studies built into the degree. The programme is bilingual: it starts mainly in English and shifts toward Finnish as it advances, and it is designed for students whose first language is not Finnish. It meets the requirements of Finland's early childhood education law, so you qualify as an early childhood education social pedagogue. Graduates can work in early childhood education, child protection, schools, youth work, private companies and non-profit organisations.

name: Textile and Material Engineering
overview: You study textile materials and manufacturing processes from fibres to finished products, with textile recycling, the circular economy, industrial economics, quality management, supply chain and project management, on a base of mathematics, chemistry and physics. Electives span business, entrepreneurship and environmental engineering. Teaching combines contact teaching, online learning, project work, laboratory exercises and industry collaboration, with mandatory practical training and exchange or overseas internships available. Everything is taught in English, with attention to the changing textile and fashion sector. Graduates work in production, product development, quality assurance and supply chains.

name: Media and Arts
overview: In the first year you pick one of three tracks, Interactive Media, Music and Event Production, or Fine Art Lab, with further modules in game design, sound design and fine art photography. You build a personal curriculum from the study modules, combining your specialisation with electives, and learn to develop ideas into finished products that succeed artistically, technically and economically. Practical training and exchange studies abroad are part of the offer. The programme is based at Mediapolis, a media campus that houses companies including the broadcaster YLE. Graduates work as experts, developers and entrepreneurs in games, music and live events, new media, service design and art galleries.

name: Chemistry, Science and Engineering
overview: You study organic, inorganic, physical, analytical and materials chemistry together with physics, mathematics and computational methods, taking an interdisciplinary approach to scientific problems. Teaching combines theory with hands-on experimentation, collaborative projects, laboratory exercises and research-oriented coursework, and in the second year you can join active research groups through research training placements. The programme draws on the university's Chemistry and Advanced Materials research centre. Graduates work in research institutions, high-technology industries, pharmaceuticals and environmental consulting, and the degree continues into master's programmes in chemistry and materials science without reapplication.

name: Engineering Physics, Science and Engineering
overview: You study the principles behind physical phenomena together with mathematics, modelling and computation, building foundations in mathematics, natural sciences and engineering in the first year before specialising in engineering physics with electives. Three focus areas are available: aerosol physics, computational physics and photonics. Teaching combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, and second-year students can join research groups for hands-on research experience. Graduates work in research, technology development, engineering design and data analysis, and the degree continues into master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

name: Environmental Engineering, Science and Engineering
overview: The first year covers mathematics, natural sciences and engineering, after which you specialise in environmental engineering: water treatment, wastewater management, resource efficiency, circular economy solutions, environmental monitoring, life cycle assessment and environmental modelling. You choose a minor that matches your interests, and learn through projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, with research training placements available in the second year. Graduates work in environmental consulting, water and wastewater management, sustainable industry, environmental technology development and research, and the degree continues into master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

name: Materials Science, Science and Engineering
overview: You study how the structure of materials shapes their properties and performance, and how to design materials for specific uses, drawing on chemistry, physics and engineering for applications in renewable energy, medical devices, electronics and sustainable manufacturing. Teaching combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, in small multicultural groups using modern laboratory equipment and digital tools, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates work in high-tech manufacturing, energy solutions, research, product development and sustainability innovation, or continue directly to master's programmes at the same university.

name: Administrative Sciences, Sustainable Urban Development
overview: You study administrative sciences with attention to societal change and governance, in a programme that brings together urban development and sustainability across three specialisations: Administrative Sciences, Social Sciences and Technology. A challenge-based Urban Lab course puts students from the specialisations in teams on real urban development projects with organisations such as the City of Tampere. Graduates work in city organisations responsible for urban development and international affairs, in research projects and in companies focused on urban planning, with study rights to the master's programme in transformative urban and regional governance.

name: Social Sciences, Sustainable Urban Development
overview: You study social sciences with a focus on societal change and how it affects wellbeing, equity, participation and environmental sustainability, within a programme that offers three specialisations: Administrative Sciences, Social Sciences and Technology. A challenge-based Urban Lab course puts you in interdisciplinary teams with local planners and citizens on real urban development projects with organisations such as the City of Tampere. Graduates work in public sector, city and regional organisations on development, planning and international affairs, or in research, and continue to the master's programme in social science research, in Transforming Societies or Comparative Social Policy and Welfare.

name: Technology, Sustainable Urban Development
overview: You study technological and civil engineering solutions for sustainable built environments, in a programme that shares its Urban Lab course and its three specialisations (Technology, Administrative Sciences and Social Sciences) with students from other fields. In the challenge-based Urban Lab you work in interdisciplinary teams with local planners and citizens on real urban development projects with the City of Tampere and other organisations, and the degree ends with a thesis. Graduates have found work in city organisations, academia and engineering and technology companies, and continue to the master's programme in civil engineering with an urban systems focus.

name: Socially Sustainable Societies
overview: You examine well-being and health, past and present, through the social sciences, with themes in public health, urban studies and global social policy: welfare institutions, social protection, intergenerational justice and the reduction of inequality by income, gender, ethnicity, age and place. Teaching builds on the faculty's current research, and free-choice courses from other programmes let you broaden the degree. The programme takes a Nordic view of social sustainability and the welfare state. Graduates work in the public sector, corporations and non-governmental organisations, and continue to the master's tracks in Transforming Societies or Comparative Social Policy and Welfare.

name: Bachelor's and Master's Degree Programme in Data Engineering
overview: You study computer science, mathematics and engineering together with the legal, ethical and economic sides of data, with a focus on data technologies across the whole pipeline, from collecting and storing data to analysing it. Through freely chosen minor studies you can lean towards data storage, data analysis or machine learning. A bachelor's thesis and an internship are part of the degree, and the master's thesis is typically practical work done in a company. The three-year bachelor's flows directly into the two-year master's within the same programme, and it is taught on the Joensuu and Kuopio campuses.

name: Bachelor's and Master's Degree Programme in Information Technology
overview: You study basic and advanced programming, algorithms, data management, software design and human-computer interaction, and add one or two minor subjects such as data science, business, law, social sciences or environmental sciences. Teaching is on campus in Joensuu and Kuopio, with some courses shared with a local university of applied sciences, and some companies offer internships and thesis placements. The university works actively with local IT companies, and the bachelor's flows directly into the master's within the programme. Graduates are aimed at careers in Finnish ICT companies, with research options and a doctoral programme open for those who want them.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in East Slavic Societies and Religion
overview: You choose one of two majors with shared foundations: East Slavic Languages and Cultures, leading to a Bachelor of Arts, or Orthodox Theology, leading to a Bachelor of Theology. The studies cover Russian and Ukrainian language, East Slavic cultural studies, Orthodox theology and the part religion plays in society, taking an interdisciplinary approach that joins humanities and theology and builds practical language skills and intercultural competence through work with original sources. Pathways suit both native speakers and learners of the languages. Graduates are prepared for work in education, public administration, international organisations, journalism and civil society.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Lifelong Learning and Sustainable Development
overview: You study education and learning across the life course, looking at how learning supports social and cultural sustainability: education policy and systems, adult education, active citizenship and non-formal education, as well as statistical and qualitative research methods. Teaching includes project-based learning and service learning with working-life organisations, an internship and a bachelor's thesis with a preparatory seminar. The focus is on learning in associations, workplaces, organisations and civic movements rather than on classroom teacher training. Graduates can work in educational planning and policy, development projects and adult education, or continue to one of the university's international master's programmes.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Social Sciences
overview: You study sociology and social and public policy, with themes such as labour, education, care, multiculturalism and information technology, and ask how wellbeing, alienation and culture shape society and its policies. Courses are taught through lectures, seminars and reading groups, with assessment by learning journals, essays and exams, and you learn methods for collecting and analysing data on current social issues. A minor subject lets you widen the degree. Delivery is hybrid and does not require you to be on campus, which makes this the only bachelor's programme in social science in Finland taught in English.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Urban Sustainability Studies
overview: You study cities and sustainability across the social sciences, natural sciences, technical sciences and humanities, and build your own profile with three minors chosen from over 20 themes such as Urban Ecology, Sustainable Business, Smart Cities, Urban Health and Wellbeing and Post-growth Cities. The first year is at the home university, and the second and third are spent at two or more partner universities in Europe within a joint degree run by ten universities, with a mix of on-site and online courses and work on real sustainability challenges with students, teachers and businesses. The degree ends with a bachelor's thesis.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
overview: The programme combines disciplines that are usually studied apart. A common core of courses teaches you how the disciplines relate and how to work interdisciplinary, and disciplinary modules of growing depth are combined into one of six specialisations: Data Science, Digital Humanities, Ecology and Adaptation, Economics of Natural Resources, Resource Management of Global Forests, or Social Data Science. The degree finishes with a thesis seminar and bachelor's thesis, and Finnish language and communication studies can be added. The aim is skills in analysis, problem-solving and critical thinking, and graduates typically continue to a master's programme.

name: Science
overview: You study mathematics and statistics, physics, chemistry, and computer and data science, with a shared foundation in university-level mathematics and basic programming in the first semester. After that you choose one of four study tracks, each with compulsory basic and intermediate studies, and you can specialise in it or combine two or three tracks through electives for a more interdisciplinary degree. Such degrees typically include lectures, exercises and laboratory or computing work, and end with a bachelor's thesis. The bachelor's leads to master's studies, and graduates usually go on to work in research and modern technology fields.

name: Computer Science and Engineering
overview: You study programming, hardware, software, artificial intelligence and data processing, supported by engineering mathematics including matrix analysis, statistics and probability. You choose a major from Artificial Intelligence, Applied Computing, Computer Engineering and Cyber Security. Teaching mixes theory with exercises and projects modelled on real technology challenges, taught by industry experts, with internship opportunities in global ICT companies and a Super Fab Lab for prototyping and fabrication. The university works with companies such as Nokia, Oura and Mediatek, and master's studies in the same field follow on automatically. Graduates are sought by corporations, small companies and startups.

name: Electronics and Communications Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, physics and signal processing, then professional courses in electronics design, computer engineering and programming, measurement techniques, electronic components and materials, and telecommunications. You specialise in Electronics Design, Electronics Materials and Components, Future Electronics and Measurement Techniques, Telecommunication, or Radio Engineering. Theory is paired with practical work in a Super Fab Lab for prototyping and fabrication and in test environments such as the 6G test network and SmartCampus. The programme sits within Oulu's technology cluster, which hosts the 6G Flagship research programme, and leads to master's programmes in electronics or wireless communications engineering.

name: Software Engineering and Information Systems
overview: The curriculum is built from five modules: Introduction, Software Development, Programming, Humans, Organisation and Design of Information Systems, and a Capstone Project that closes the degree. You learn to build technology and also to lead teams and manage projects, with an emphasis on user-centred design, and optional minors can come from humanities, business or technologies such as virtual reality, the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence. Oulu has a strong technology scene with events, hackathons and networking. Graduates work as software developers, UX designers or project managers, and the bachelor's continues automatically into the master's.

name: International Business Management
overview: You study international business management theories, the Nordic business context, sustainable business management and creative entrepreneurship, along with some Finnish language for the working environment, and electives from other disciplines such as ICT. Teaching combines theory with practical assignments carried out with organisations, internship courses that introduce the local business ecosystem, especially high-tech and health-tech, and work in intercultural teams on real business scenarios. The business school holds AACSB accreditation. Graduates qualify for the English-taught master's in international business management and work as business development managers, management consultants, sales directors or entrepreneurs.

name: Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering
overview: You study programming, data analysis, mathematical modelling and intelligent systems on a base of mathematics and physics, and choose a major in Information Technology, Electrical Engineering or Computational Data Analysis, with specialisations such as signal processing and machine learning, software development, power engineering, communications or embedded systems. Teaching mixes theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. The bachelor's continues directly into master's programmes at the same university, towards fields such as machine learning, telecommunications and renewable energy.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Human and Planetary Health
overview: You study human biology and health (anatomy, physiology, pathology, microbiology, nutrition and pharmacology), global and planetary health (environmental health, public health, climate and health) and health promotion and disease prevention, linking the molecular, individual and population levels. Teaching uses lectures, seminars and laboratory work, with a bachelor's thesis, optional practical training and project work, and Finnish language studies throughout. Four university departments run the programme on the Kuopio campus. Graduates work in public health, health promotion and planetary health in NGOs, policy bodies and research, or continue to master's studies in toxicology or public health.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Sustainable Forest Bioeconomy
overview: You study forest ecology, biodiversity and management, forest mensuration and remote sensing, forest technology, wood science, economics and policy, with a distinctive emphasis on information and communication technology for sustainable forest management. The first year covers fundamentals and methods, the second sustainable management, and the third regional development, networking and an exchange period, with field work, a professional internship and a bachelor's thesis. You choose a minor such as computer science, sustainable business or environmental policy. Graduates become foresters, forest data scientists, GIS analysts or policy experts, or continue to master's programmes in European or transatlantic forestry.

name: Bachelor's Degree Programme in Sustainable and Social Entrepreneurship
overview: You study business, sustainability and languages, with entrepreneurship as the major and a specialisation in sustainable and social business, examining societal, environmental and economic problems through analytical frameworks. Learning is research-based and team-based, with real cases, interactive work with businesses and presentations; in the third year you write a thesis on an entrepreneurship topic of your choice, and internships are encouraged. The programme links to the Futures Research Centre and to partners such as Abo Akademi and Turku University of Applied Sciences. Graduates work as entrepreneurs, managers of regenerative businesses or experts in third-sector organisations, or continue to master's studies.

name: Degree Programme in Information and Communication Technology
overview: You study programming and embedded systems design, software engineering and development processes, microprocessors, operating systems, networks, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, with a focus on practical application and communication, and an optional minor in entrepreneurship. Teaching is contact teaching in modules, and the bachelor's thesis is a personal project that may be done with companies. Exchange studies and internships abroad run through the European 28DIGITAL consortium, and you can include modules from different units to build your own profile. Graduates work as software engineers, architects, project managers, security specialists or ICT consultants, with direct entry to the master's in ICT.
